title: Delta-driven incremental maintenance of a transitive closure under insertions versus PostgreSQL recomputation on the updated edges
explanation: The case has three phases over an edge set that is split into a base part EBase and an inserted delta EDelta. Phase 1 is the naive fixpoint computation of TOld, the transitive closure of EBase alone. Phase 2 is a hand-written delta-driven maintainer modelled on DBSP/Feldera/Materialize-style incremental view maintenance: it seeds Delta with the consequences of the inserted edges against the already-known old closure (EDelta together with TOld composed with EDelta, minus what TOld already has) and then repeatedly extends only that delta by joining it with the whole new edge set EBase ∪ EDelta, folding the result into T, until the delta is empty — the old view TOld is never recomputed. Phase 3 recomputes the closure Res of EBase ∪ EDelta from scratch via PostgreSQL's recursive-union rounds. The Hoare triple's claim T = Res is the correctness statement for incremental view maintenance under an insertion: propagating only the change from the old fixpoint yields the same relation as recomputing the closure of the updated edge set from scratch.
preInWords: The precondition is simply true; no constraints are placed on EBase, EDelta, or their relationship.
postInWords: T, the closure obtained by seeding from the old closure TOld and propagating only the delta caused by the inserted edges EDelta, equals Res, the closure of EBase ∪ EDelta recomputed from scratch by PostgreSQL's recursive-union rounds.
family: production algorithm pair (dependent phases, rate mismatch)
obstructionExpectation: dependent phases (the maintainer reads the finished old view) and rate mismatch (delta rounds count edges after the first inserted edge, recomputation rounds count path length); leveled-framework target; with prophecy both containments follow from the fixpoint facts (no leastness needed)

hand-written: PostgreSQL ExecRecursiveUnion rounds (legacy Example2037) on EBase ∪ EDelta
schemaLinking: same schema on both sides; direct equality of the computed relations
